text:
The evidence can't tell us that. It shows tree-cover loss, not its cause.

What it does show: Hansen/UMD mapped about 13.5 ha of tree-cover loss in 2025, roughly 3.9% of the 345.6 ha property. Nearly all of it (about 13.1 ha) was native forest according to the 2021 MGAP map, and the JRC 2020 map agrees it was forest (98% of the area). No planted forest was involved.

What it doesn't show:
- Whether the land was cleared for agriculture. Hansen loss includes any stand replacement, such as harvest, fire, storm, or clearing, and it doesn't record land use afterward.
- Whether the change is persistent. 2025 is the latest year in the series, so the loss is still pending corroboration and needs a later year of data.
- Whether it was legal or who was responsible.

To test the agricultural-clearing hypothesis, you would need later imagery or land-cover data showing what replaced the forest, or fire and storm records for the same area.
